gap: No result ChatGPT got states an instrument measurement for any of these screens: the only one I could open is Parkablogs' 152 nits maximum and 68% sRGB on the 13.3-inch Duex Plus (the pre-DS model) against the maker's 300-nit figure, and no named reviewer I could open has put any candidate on a scale.
standout_why: Compared against the Mobile Pixels Duex Plus technical specification page, the PCWorld Shop Duex Lite listing and thedadsneeze.com's roundup (the cited mobilepixels.us Duex DS page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt). The first two give only maker specs (300 nits, 4.5 W, 1.3 lb). thedadsneeze calls itself 'a researched roundup, not a hands-on test' and already calls the Duex Plus DS and Max DS dim at an unsourced 250 nits, so rivals have the verdict but not a measurement. The finding is thin: one reviewer, an unnamed calibrator, a 2022 unit of the predecessor model, and nothing measured on weight, which is what the question turns on.
decides: It does not change the pick. With no named scale reading for any candidate, the under-2 lb ranking has to rest on maker-stated weights, labelled as such, which is the same caveat ChatGPT gave. The brightness measurement only adds a caveat to the Duex Plus DS row: the earlier Duex Plus measured about half its 300-nit claim, and the DS model has no measurement I could open.

unsourced: RTINGS' measured brightness, contrast, sRGB coverage and weight for the Mobile Pixels DUEX Plus: the review, the DUEX Plus vs TRIO comparison and the review-updates page all returned only navigation text. A search summary gave 185 nits, which I did not use.

Tom's Hardware's measurements for the SideTrak Swivel 12.5-inch: the page returned only menus at four offsets and the inkl.com mirror returned 403. A search summary gave 301.4 nits, 72.4% sRGB, 51.3% DCI-P3 and a 1.3 lb spec weight, none of which I could open.

Mobile Pixels' own weights and today's prices for the Duex Plus DS and Duex Max DS: mobilepixels.us returned HTTP 429 to the product page (twice), the collection page and storecheck.py, so the 1.3 lb and 1.8 lb figures are not re-read by me today.

A scale reading by a named reviewer for the Duex Plus DS, Duex Max DS, Duex Lite or SideTrak Swivel, with or without magnets and cable: two searches and the reviews I opened turned up only repeated maker figures.
Any instrument measurement of the DS-generation panels (Duex Plus DS, Duex Max DS): Root-Nation's Duex Max DS review returned 403, and the other DS reviews I found repeat the 300-nit spec.

Gadget Review's 178-nit, 185-nit and 60 to 64.4% sRGB figures for the Duex Plus (https://www.gadgetreview.com/mobile-pixels-duex-plus-review): the page credits no tester, so I left them out as unattributed.

SideTrak's and Xebec's own US pages for the weight and price of the Swivel and Tri-Screen 2, and any named measurement of the Xebec, KOJOM, Tlscon or Limink ET14: not reached within the tool-call budget.
